title: flake: a call in a chat of more than two was created, not refused
description:
Seen once in a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features` run on
2026-11-26, in crates/mimid-agent/tests/vtc.rs:685
(a_call_in_a_chat_of_more_than_two_is_refused). Passes 3 of 3 alone and
2 of 2 as a whole test file, so it only shows under the parallel
workspace run.

## What happened

The test pushes carol and dave into the chat's `participants`, so a call
would hold three, then creates a VTCCall and expects `notCreated` with
`invalidProperties`. The run got a created call instead:
`"created":{"k":{...,"activeParticipantCount":1,...}}` and
`"notCreated":null`.

So the serving path saw a chat with two participants or fewer at the
moment it checked.

## The two readings, neither ruled out

1. Test: the mutation through `alice.store.state()` is not durably
   visible to the serving path by the time the POST is handled, and the
   test only usually wins that race.
2. Product: the VTC create path reads a participant list captured
   earlier -- a snapshot or a cache -- rather than the current one, and
   under load the stale copy is what it checks.

Reading 2 is why this is P1 rather than a test annoyance. The assertion
is a policy refusal: a call in a group chat being allowed because the
participant count read low is a real defect, and the same stale read
would affect any other check over `participants`.

## Next step

Find what the create path reads `participants` from and whether it can
be older than the last committed write. If it reads through the same
store handle the test writes to, the race is the test's and the fix is
to make the write observable before the POST. If it reads a cached
snapshot, the bead is a product bug and needs a regression test that
fails before the fix.

Do not "fix" this by raising a timeout or retrying the assertion: both
readings would stay.

Related: bead mimid-gn1w is a different flake in the same full-workspace
runs (an SSE subscribe that does not establish). Same trigger --
parallel load -- different mechanism.

## Diagnosed 2026-11-26: reading 1, the test, and not a product bug

Three facts, each checked in the code:

1. `Store::state` returns a `MutexGuard<'_, State>` (store.rs:604),
   a live lock over shared state. There is no snapshot or cache, so the
   test's mutation is visible to every later reader. Reading 2's
   "serving path reads a captured participant list" is therefore out.
2. The create path reads participants fresh inside the check
   (vtc_backend.rs:392): it takes `state()`, looks up the parent room
   and counts `parent.others(user)`.
3. `Store::sync` REPLACES a room's participants outright --
   `room.participants = roles.participants(&participants)` at
   sync.rs:470 and sync.rs:569 -- rebuilding them from the MLS group and
   the journal.

So the mechanism is a sync tick landing between the test pushing carol
and dave into `room.participants` and the POST that reads them. The
runner owns that field and recomputes it; the test writes to derived
state behind the runner's back, and usually wins the race. Under full
suite load the interleaving gets likelier, which matches the failure
only ever appearing there.

Not proven: I did not catch a sync tick in the act during the failure.
What would prove it is a log of the sync at that moment, or making the
race deterministic by forcing a sync between the mutation and the POST
and watching the test fail every time.

## The fix

Stop writing to `room.participants` from the test. Either build a chat
that genuinely has three participants, or run the assertion against a
store with no runner syncing under it. Raising a timeout or retrying
does nothing here, since the state is being overwritten rather than
arriving late.

Dropping to P2: the reading that made this P1, a real stale read in a
policy check, is eliminated by fact 1.
design:
## Fix options, costed 2026-11-26

The test's own doc explains the shortcut: "the test sets that list
rather than standing up two more daemons". The shortcut is what breaks,
because Store::sync owns room.participants and recomputes it from the
MLS group (sync.rs:470, sync.rs:569). The likely trigger is the room's
own creation echoing back -- create_room then save puts it on the
server, a sync tick pulls it back, and the record is rebuilt from the
group, which has no carol or dave.

1. **Real members.** Add carol and dave to the group so the list is
   authoritative and sync recomputes the same thing. The durable fix and
   the only one that tests what the ceiling actually reads. Costs what
   the test avoided: identities and KeyPackages for two more users, if
   not two more daemons.
2. **Wait for the echo-back, then push.** Push the participants only
   after the room has been synced once, so the push is the last write
   and nothing else arrives to overwrite it. Cheap, but there is no
   observable for "synced once": the record can look identical before
   and after, and `Control::until` polls a request count, not a store
   record. Would need a condition worth trusting first.
3. **Make the overwrite loud.** Keep the shortcut, and after the POST,
   if the call was created, assert the participants still hold carol.
   Does not fix the flake; converts a silent wrong-pass into a failure
   that names the cause. Cheapest, and worth doing whichever other
   option is taken, because a test that can be overwritten into passing
   is worse than one that fails.

Recommended: 3 now, 1 when someone is in the harness anyway. Not 2 --
it trades a visible race for an invisible dependence on an observable
that does not exist.

Do not raise a timeout: the list is overwritten, not late, so patience
changes nothing. This bead is NOT part of mimid-zr08's deadline group
for that reason.
